method: Cable swaps done by the user with the FNK0099 USB-UART kept connected. For each cable: three UART-reset starts (the resetting UART open, SFC stays powered, 25 s each, no user action), then three cold power-ons (USB-UART unplugged at the Mac for 13.1-21.5 s, non-resetting attach 0.018-0.027 s after the port returned, user pressed Right then B about 20 s later).

results.cable: direct USB-C to USB-C (the same cable used with the first controller)

cold_power_on.inputs: Right 0x080 and B 0x001 pressed and released in every run

results.cable: USB-C to USB-A cable plus USB-A to USB-C adapter (the older assembly)

cold_power_on.inputs: Right 0x080 and B 0x001 pressed and released in every run
cold_power_on.observation: In c2old-P3, B was recorded as three press/release pairs within about 0.4 s (held 20, 290 and 50 ms). This may be a light press or contact bounce on the second controller's B button; the Host logs the reports as received. Not investigated.

common_sequence_in_all_12_starts.event: RECOVERY note=initial_attach; root port powered at uptime 1155 ms

unplug_observation: When the user unplugged the second controller (keyboard open) to change cables after c2cc-P3, the same single line 'E USB HOST: EP command error: ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE' appeared as in the first-controller R2 unplug, followed by HID disconnect close ESP_OK, mask 0x000 reason=disconnect and USB library flags=0x2.
interpretation: The delayed first enumeration also enumerated the second controller on every attached start, with both cables and both start types (12/12), at the same timings as the first controller. Together with the first controller (C-to-C: 10/10 plus 3/3 physical RESET), the effect is not specific to one unit or cable among those tried. Sample sizes remain small, and the minimum sufficient delay is unknown.
